messages:
maria: Heads up — ran into a nasty rotation edge where our CLI/sampleapp keeps using an old project-scoped key after we set the new ORG-scoped key in the env. long-lived streams reconnect and pollute metrics. anyone seen similar?
ben: hmm can you paste the env + command you used?
maria: repro:
```
# container env (in k8s init):
export REDWOOD_API_KEY_PROJECT=proj-old-xxx
export REDWOOD_API_KEY_ORG=org-new-yyy
# app startup sets env to ORG key later via sidecar
./bin/redwood-cli run --sampleapp
```
Output shows requests authenticated as proj-old-xxx after restart. :facepalm:
jess: quick thought — do you have any credential cache on disk? the SDK historically prefers a credential file over env vars in some versions.
sam: yep, older go/python sdks wrote ~/.redwood/credentials and that had precedence. If the process picks up that file at init it will ignore subsequent env rotations.
maria: whoa — that would explain it. our k8s job injects env after container bootstrap via a sidecar update, but we never clear any local cache.
ben: can you check for file presence in the container? `ls -la ~/.redwood` and `cat ~/.redwood/credentials` (masking)
maria: checked — file exists. contains project key. we were assuming env overrides file.
jess: that's UX bug territory — SDK/CLI should either: 1) prefer env vars always, or 2) warn when file creds and env creds disagree. At minimum log a one-line warning.
sam: agreed. quick mitigation: add a startup hook in the sampleapp/container that nukes ~/.redwood/credentials on rotation, or update the init script to reconcile. Longer term: change precedence in SDK 2.x and add a deprecation warning in 1.x.
maria: I'll patch our automation for now. open to a public fix though — this will bite other customers who rely on injected env rotation.
ben: filed a tiny RFC/issue: https://intern.redwood/issue/DEVEX-4523 — proposing env > file precedence and a CLI warning when mismatch. tagging @eng-runtime for impact. :eyes:
jess: small CLI change: when starting, if env key set and file exists and differs, print `WARNING: REDWOOD_API_KEY_* differs from cached credentials — environment overrides cached credentials but cached file may be stale. Consider clearing ~/.redwood/credentials or restarting.`
devex-bot: Created issue DEVEX-4523 and linked to repo redwood/cli (PR template suggested).
maria: thanks — will test and push our fix. can someone add a short note in onboarding docs about this precedence? it's a surprising gotcha for sample apps.
sam: adding to docs backlog. also adding e2e test for rotation in sampleapp repo so it fails if env rotation doesn't change outgoing auth.
ben: ok assigning to @jess for the CLI warning PR and @sam for docs + e2e. I'll follow-up on runtime changes after triage.
jess: will open PR today, small change + unit test.
maria: great, saved us a pager at least. :thumbsup:
